protections: The duck-typed buffer predicate must invoke `constructor.isBuffer` only when that member is callable, so an object carrying an own `constructor` whose `isBuffer` is truthy but not a function is classified as not-a-buffer instead of being called (lib/utils.js:327-333, reached from lib/stringify.js:134).

`qs.parse` drops keys that name Object.prototype members (`constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, ...) unless `allowPrototypes` or `plainObjects` is opted into, so default-parsed output cannot carry an own `constructor` key (lib/parse.js:235, lib/parse.js:250, lib/parse.js:292; exercised at test/parse.js:453-458).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The throw is only reachable through qs.stringify, and the project's threat model states that stringify's input object is the calling application's own data, not an untrusted channel (.github/THREAT_MODEL.md:28), so the caller is expected to sanitize its own objects.

utils.isBuffer is an internal helper with exactly one in-repo caller (lib/stringify.js:134), so guarding that call site removes the observable crash; the deep-require export at lib/utils.js:375 is not a documented API (package.json:13 makes lib/index.js the package main).

parse output is ordinary data: `allowPrototypes`/`plainObjects` deliberately preserve every key (test/parse.js:416, test/parse.js:1050), so parse must not be changed and the consumer-side predicate is the only correct place to fix it; parse merely hands the check a shape it never inspects.

Buffer values are already covered by the existing suite (test/stringify.js:929-933, test/utils.js:597-614), so a solver can assume the buffer branch is settled and only think about the hostile shape, then over-harden the test.

dist/qs.js is a gitignored build output (.gitignore:7) regenerated by `npm run dist` at prepack (package.json:72, package.json:82); editing lib and rebuilding covers it, and no test imports dist (all suites require '../' or '../lib/utils').

conflicts.what: The natural guard for T1 must reject a truthy non-callable `constructor.isBuffer` while still returning true for SaferBuffer/Buffer instances (test/stringify.js:929-933, test/utils.js:607-612) and false for `{ constructor: Buffer }` (test/utils.js:604-605); a blanket rejection of objects with an own `constructor` key, or replacing the duck-type with Buffer.isBuffer/instanceof Buffer, satisfies T1's shape but changes the buffer path and breaks the Buffer-less/browserified use the duck-type exists for (test/stringify.js:940-948, CHANGELOG.md:782).

Closing T3 at the producer (dropping `constructor` keys in parse even under plainObjects/allowPrototypes) would contradict documented option behaviour exercised by test/parse.js:416 and test/parse.js:1050, while the single predicate fix at lib/utils.js:332 closes both T1 and T3.

fairness_risks: A security rule that stringify must refuse any object with an own `constructor` key would reject legitimate data: `constructor` is an ordinary key, parse preserves it under allowPrototypes/plainObjects (lib/parse.js:217, lib/parse.js:292; test/parse.js:416, test/parse.js:1050), and round-tripping parse output through stringify is an explicit non-security goal (.github/THREAT_MODEL.md:78).

A rule that the buffer predicate may rely on the global `Buffer` (Buffer.isBuffer or instanceof) would refuse/regress browserified and Buffer-less environments, which is exactly why the constructor duck-type exists (CHANGELOG.md:782, test/stringify.js:940-948).

A rule that rejects `constructor`-bearing buffer values (SaferBuffer/Buffer instances) would break the must-keep-working stringification in test/stringify.js:929-933 and the direct predicate expectations in test/utils.js:597-614.
Tightening parse's prototype-key guard so `constructor` is dropped even under `plainObjects` would refuse keys that test/parse.js:1050 and test/parse.js:416 require to survive.

design.why: Only two independent fix sites exist in the pinned snapshot, and one of them (T5, dist/qs.js:14) is a gitignored browserify artifact that prepack regenerates (package.json:72, package.json:82), so it is a correct skip rather than a scored trap. T1/T2/T3/T4 all collapse to one edit at lib/utils.js:332: the same callable test closes the stringify call site, the deep-require export, the parse-produced `constructor` shape and the coupled buffer requirement. That is one independent decision, below the 3-5 group target, and its only depth comes from the dismissal in .github/THREAT_MODEL.md:28. Note the reachable shape is a *nested* value only: the module entry at lib/stringify.js:292-362 never passes the root object to isBuffer, so a test input must be at least one level deep (e.g. { x: { constructor: { isBuffer: 'y' } } }) or come from parse with plainObjects/allowPrototypes. If the pipeline wants a stacked task here it would have to use the screener's injection room (a sibling `obj.constructor.isTypedArray` predicate beside isBuffer at lib/stringify.js:134, a second isBuffer call site in parse at lib/parse.js:397, or a constructor-driven isRegExp beside lib/utils.js:323-325); those are author-planted code, not published defects, and planted siblings are the easy tier.
